BURHAN:v2p7/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p7/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p7/r4.claim: Conditional expressions whose response is a request or command are general; the author illustrates this with two commands following إذا.
BURHAN:v2p7/r4.anchor: هذا إذا كان الجواب طلبا مثل هاتين الآيتين

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.claim: When stubborn people engage in frivolous argument and mockery, the Prophet should leave them and speak only when they are receptive.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.anchor: When he sees that they are indulging in frivolous arguments and mockery, he should leave them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.claim: The Prophet's responsibility is preaching, not coercing belief; he should disregard new demands and give his warning through the Qur'an in the best way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p49/.anchor: His responsibility is just to preach and deliver the message. He is not responsible for their faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.claim: Khawḍ literally concerns entering into something and idiomatically means frivolous talk, hair-splitting, and baseless criticism that dismisses a subject by ridicule; the author cites Qur'anic usage including 9:65.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.anchor: It means to engage in frivolous talk, hair-splitting and baseless criticism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.claim: The wording about treating religion as sport clarifies the point of khawḍ in these verses; the author also points to 4:140 as an explanation of the word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p51/.anchor: In other words after mentioning the word, its purpose has been elucidated.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: Islahi reads the instruction as forbidding believers to remain where revelation is rejected or mocked until the discussion changes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: wherever you hear that God’s revelations are being rejected and ridiculed, do not sit there with them until they get engaged in some other talk

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: Although the singular address appears directed to the Prophet, it reaches all believers through him; the next verse and 4:140 establish its general scope.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: in reality it is directed to all the believers through him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: Preaching to opponents in a frenzy only intensifies their agitation, so Muslims should wait until they return to normal before presenting Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: presenting that very thing before him in this condition will only enhance his frenzy and hysteria

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: Remaining silent when someone openly speaks nonsense against God and the Messenger is incompatible with a preacher’s honour and support for truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: not only fighting with him is wrong for a preacher, but also remaining silent for him is inapt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: Defending truth is a sign of faith; tolerating humiliation of God, the Messenger, Qur’an, and sharia can gradually lead to hypocrisy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: This weakness of faith can ultimately lead a person in a gradual way to hypocrisy

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.claim: The reference to al-Nisāʾ explains the honour aspect: hypocrites were reprimanded for joining gatherings where revelation was mocked despite being forbidden to do so.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p52/.anchor: the hypocrites are reprimanded for participating in the gatherings of the rivals where God’s revelations were openly made fun of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.claim: When conversation turns to mockery, believers should leave even if they fear rivals will ridicule them for abandoning a polemical debate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.anchor: if he now leaves that place his rivals will ridicule him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.claim: Staying out of deference to a gathering shows lost religious honour; one would not stay silent if parents were abused, while duty to God is greater.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.anchor: the obligation he owes to God and His directives is much greater than his obligation to his parents

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.claim: Continuing a debate to prove truth becomes ego when corrupted minds will only grow angrier; it harms truth, so the believer should recognize Satan’s ploy and leave.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.anchor: such an engagement merely becomes a question of one’s ego. It will not be helpful for the cause of truth at all

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.claim: If Satan tricks believers into such a gathering, they should leave as soon as they recognize their mistake, while remaining vigilant against deception.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.anchor: they should leave the gathering as soon as they realize their folly

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.claim: Mockers of God’s revelations are especially unjust to themselves, and believers cannot know when God may punish hypocrites for keeping their company.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p53/.anchor: those who make fun of God’s revelations are the ones who are the most unjust to their souls

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p54/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p54/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p54/.claim: The discourse gradually clarifies that the previous verse’s singular address is directed to the believers generally.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p54/.anchor: though in the previous verse the address was singular, but the discourse was directed at the believers

MAJAZ:v1p194/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p194/r1.claim: Al-dhikrā and al-dhikr are the same word.

NAHHAS:v2p72/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p72/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p72/r8.claim: The command to turn away concerns people disputing God's signs through denial, rebuttal, and mockery; the Prophet is to disapprove and leave until they discuss something else.
NAHHAS:v2p72/r8.anchor: التقدير وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا بالتكذيب والرد والاستهزاء ( فأعرض عنهم ) منكرا عليهم

NAHHAS:v2p72/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p72/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p72/r9.claim: God disciplines the Prophet, who sat with polytheists to admonish and invite them while they mocked the Quran, by ordering a disapproving withdrawal.
NAHHAS:v2p72/r9.anchor: فأدب الله جل وعز نبيه فهذا صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه كان يقعد إلى قوم من المشركين يعظهم ويدعوهم

NAHHAS:v2p72/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p72/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p72/r10.claim: This verse refutes those who claim authoritative Imams and followers may associate with sinners and approve their opinions as dissimulation.
NAHHAS:v2p72/r10.anchor: وكان في هذا رد في كتاب الله عز وجل على من زعم أن الأئمة الذين هم حجج واتباعهم لهم

NAHHAS:v2p72/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p72/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن عامر
NAHHAS:v2p72/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads وإما ينسينك with a form indicating intensification.
NAHHAS:v2p72/r11.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عامر ( وإما ينسينك الشيطان ) على التكثير

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r36.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r36.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r36.claim: Satan makes evil deeds seem fair, causes people to forget God’s commands, and even attempts to alter revelation.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r36.anchor: causing them to forget God and His commandments (6:68; 12:42; 18:63; 58:19); and even by attempting to alter revelation (22:52).

TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r3.speaker: عبد الأعلى بن أعين
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says believers should not sit where an imam is insulted or a Muslim is backbitten, citing the command to turn away from mockery of God's verses.
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r3.anchor: بإسناده عن عبد الأعلى بن أعين قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says not to sit with people of disputation, whom he identifies as those who delve into God's verses.
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r4.anchor: عن أبي جعفر قال لا تجالسوا أهل الخصومات فإنهم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله

TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r5.speaker: محمد بن على
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r5.claim: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī identifies people driven by their own desires as those who delve into God's verses.
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن على قال إن أصحاب الأهواء من الذين يخوضون في آيات الله

TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r6.claim: A report from Abū Jaʿfar glosses delving as discussion about God and disputation over the Qur'an, and says storytellers are among those who continue other talk.
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r6.anchor: عن ربعي بن عبد الله عمن ذكره عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says these reports generalize the verse by applying its underlying rationale.
TABATABAI:6:56-73#21/r7.anchor: والروايات - كما ترى - تعمم الآية وهو أخذ بالملاك

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r1.claim: إذا is accusative by its response فأعرض, meaning ‘turn away from them at that time.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r1.anchor: " إذا " منصوب بجوابها وهو " فأعرض " أي: أعرض عنهم في هذا الوقت

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r2.claim: رأيت most plainly means visual seeing and takes one object; the present verb يخوضون already functions as a circumstantial clause, so no extra حال is needed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r2.anchor: و " رأيت " هنا تحتمل أن تكون البصرية وهو الظاهر ولذلك تعدت لواحد

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r3.claim: The Sheikh says a deleted حال is necessary: seeing them while they are engaged in digression.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا بد من تقدير حال محذوفة أي: رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا وهم خائضون فيها

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r4.claim: The author rejects that extra حال as unnecessary: يخوضون is already circumstantial, and الذين يخوضون is equivalent to الخائضين, an active participle that denotes the present.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r4.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى ذلك لأن قوله " يخوضون " مضارع والراجح حاليته، وأيضا فإن " الذين يخوضون " في قوة الخائضين

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r5.claim: A knowledge-based رأيت is possible, but the Sheikh objects that it requires deleting its second object.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون علمية، وضعفه الشيخ بأنه يلزم منه حذف المفعول الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r6.claim: Deleting the second object is forbidden if it is ellipsis by restriction, and the sounder position also forbids ellipsis for brevity; some grammarians reject the latter too.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68/r6.anchor: الصحيح المنع حتى منع ذلك بعض النحويين

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in غيره may refer to the verses, using masculine singular because الآيات means الحديث or القرآن.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه تعود على الآيات، وعاد مفردا مذكرا؛ لأن الآيات في معنى الحديث والقرآن.

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it refers to الخوض, understood from the verb: they should digress into talk other than digression, as the cited verse implies سفه from السفيه.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r2.anchor: إنها تعود على الخوض أي: المدلول عليه بالفعل

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r3.speaker: قراءة العامة
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r3.claim: The common reading uses a light sīn from أنسى, as in 18:63 and 12:42.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r3.anchor: قوله: { ينسينك } قراءة العامة: " ينسينك " بتخفيف السين من " أنساه "

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r4.claim: Ibn Amir doubles the sīn, from نسى; the verb has both causative forms, as with أنجى/نجى and أمهل/مهل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بتشديدها من " نساه " والتعدي جاء في هذا الفعل بالهمزة مرة وبالتضعيف أخرى

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r5.claim: Both readings omit the second object; though الذكر or الحق could be supplied, the author prefers ‘what you were commanded to do: leave their company after being reminded.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r5.anchor: والمفعول الثاني محذوف في القراءتين، تقديره: وإما ينسينك الشيطان الذكر أو الحق. والأحسن أن تقدر ما يليق بالمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r6.claim: They are made explicit rather than referred to by a pronoun to mark and record their quality as wrongdoers.

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r7.claim: The first condition uses إذا because their digression is certain; the second uses إن because Satan’s causing forgetfulness is possible, not inevitable, and the Prophet is protected from it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r7.anchor: وجاء الشرط الأول ب " إذا " لأن خوضهم في الآيات محقق، وفي الشرط الثاني ب " إن " لأن إنساء الشيطان له ليس أمرا محققا

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r8.claim: ذكرى is the only verbal noun on the فعلى pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r8.anchor: ولم يجيء مصدر على فعلى غير " ذكرى "

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya says إما is conditional and usually requires the emphatic heavy nūn, though it may lack it; he cites a line beginning إما يصيبك عدو.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وإما " شرط، ويلزمها في الأغلب النون الثقيلة، وقد لا تلزم

SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r10.claim: The author identifies the necessity claim as al-Zajjaj’s view and says grammarians generally disagree, citing Ibn Atiyya’s line and other poetry; no one requires specifically the heavy rather than light emphatic nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:6:68#2/r10.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره من لزوم التوكيد هو مذهب الزجاج، والناس على خلافه وأنشدوا ما أنشده ابن عطية

ASAD-NOTES:6:68#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:68#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:68#n58/r1.claim: The instruction is to leave until they immerse themselves in conversation on another subject.
ASAD-NOTES:6:68#n58/r1.anchor: Lit., "until they immerse themselves in talk other than this".

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r2.claim: All but Ibn ʿĀmir read with first nūn silent; he opens it and doubles the sīn, using the causative form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r2.anchor: كلهم قرأ وإما ينسينك الشيطان [الأنعام/ 68] بتسكين النون الأولى، وتشديد الثانية غير ابن عامر

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r3.claim: The majority reading is supported by 18:63, which uses the hamza causative for Satan causing someone to forget.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r3.anchor: الحجة لهم في قراءتهم وإما ينسينك قوله: وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir’s form is valid because doubling the middle consonant can causativize, as can hamza; faʿʿala and afʿala can interchange.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p323/r4.anchor: ووجه قول ابن عامر أنك تقول: نسيت الشيء، فإذا أردت أن غيرك أنساكه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r1.claim: The doubled sīn distinguishes a man forgetting from another causing him to forget; a prophetic saying that he was made to forget so he could establish a practice supports it.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن شدد أنه فرق بين نسي الرجل ونساه غيره واستدل بقوله عليه السلام إنما أنسى لأسن لكم فشدد لأن غيره نساه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r2.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that he forgets so that he may establish a practice for the community.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r2.anchor: واستدل بقوله عليه السلام إنما أنسى لأسن لكم فشدد لأن غيره نساه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r3.claim: The light form treats the two verb forms as interchangeable dialectal usages and cites forgetting God as leaving Him in obedience, followed by God's leaving people from reward.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن خفف أنه قال هما لغتان تستعمل إحداهما مكان الأخرى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r4.claim: One explanation of remember your Lord when you forget is remember Him when you disobey; the root sense of forgetting is leaving.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p142/r4.anchor: وقيل في قوله تعالى ﴿ واذكر ربك إذا نسيت ﴾ يريد إذا عصيت

NASHR:v2p258/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p258/r13.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p258/r13.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir geminates the sīn; the other readers lighten it.
NASHR:v2p258/r13.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر بتشديد السين، وقرأ الباقون بتخفيفها

QIRAAT-ER:6:68:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:68:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:68:18#1/r1.claim: Form II yunassiyannaka suggests repeated or intensive causing-to-forget, unlike Form IV's one-time causation.
QIRAAT-ER:6:68:18#1/r1.anchor: Form II intensive (tafʿīl) instead of Form IV — yunassiyannaka implies repeated/intensive causing-to-forget

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p211#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p211#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p211#2/r1.claim: Qatada says God forbade sitting with people who deny and mock His verses; if one forgets, one must leave after remembering.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p211#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره ﴾ قال نهاه الله تعالى أن يجلس مع الذين يخوضون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r1.claim: The command addresses the Prophet but includes believers, since the reason for the prohibition—listening to mockery of God's signs—applies to them too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r1.anchor: هذا خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدخل فيه المؤمنون لأن علة النهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r2.claim: Another view restricts the command to the Prophet because his departure and anger troubled mockers in a way that believers' departure did not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو خاص بتوحيده لأن قيامه عنهم كان يشق عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r3.claim: The addressee may instead be any listener; the mockers are variously identified as polytheists, Jews, or people of heterodox views.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r3.anchor: وقيل: خطاب للسامع والذين يخوضون المشركون أو اليهود أو أصحاب الأهواء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan takes “saw” as visual perception with one object and an omitted state: seeing the mockers while engaged in mockery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r4.anchor: ورأيت هنا بصرية ولذلك تعدت إلى واحد ولا بد من تقدير حال محذوفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r5.claim: Taking “saw” as mental knowledge is remote: it requires omitting the second object of a verb of knowing, an omission some grammarians forbid and others consider rare.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r5.anchor: وقيل: رأيت علمية لأن الخوض في الآيات ليس مما يدرك بحاسة البصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r6.claim: “Wading” in God's signs is a metaphor for mocking and attacking them; Quraysh did this in their gatherings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r6.anchor: والخوض في الآيات كناية عن الاستهزاء بها والطعن فيها. وكانت قريش في أنديتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r7.claim: Turning away means not sitting with the mockers and leaving them; it is not merely inward disapproval.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r7.anchor: فأعرض عنهم أي لا تجالسهم وقم عنهم وليس إعراضا بالقلب وحده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r8.claim: Commentators identify the quoted rule against sitting with people while God's signs are denied and mocked with this command; one may return once they change the subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r8.anchor: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r9.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r9.claim: Al-Hawfi says the pronoun refers to the mockery, as a poem shows a fool running toward foolishness when warned away from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r9.anchor: والضمير في غيره قال الحوفي عائد إلى الخوض كما قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the pronoun returns to the meaning of the signs, since they constitute talk or discourse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r10.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: إنما ذكر الهاء لأنه أعادها على معنى الآيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r11.claim: If Satan distracts the Prophet until he forgets the ban on sitting with mockers, he must not sit with them once reminded of the prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r11.anchor: أي إن شغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي عن مجالستهم فلا تقعد معهم بعد الذكرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows that Satan caused forgetfulness before the ban was revealed, since reason itself rejects sitting with mockers; once reminded, one must leave.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r12.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد وإن كان الشيطان ينسيك قبل النهي قبح مجالسة المستهزئين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r13.claim: Abu Hayyan says this reading conflicts with the apparent conditional sequence, since the command preceded the condition and both clauses describe future circumstances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r13.anchor: وهو خلاف ظاهر الشرط لأنه قد نهي عن القعود معهم قبل ثم عطف على الشرط السابق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r14.claim: The first condition uses “when” because mockery is certain, while the second uses “if” because forgetting is uncertain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r14.anchor: وما أحسن مجيء الشرط الأول بإذا التي هي للمحقق لأن كونهم يخوضون في الآيات محقق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r15.claim: Calling them wrongdoers identifies the cause of their mockery: they transgress limits and put things in the wrong places.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r15.anchor: وجاء مع القوم الظالمين تنبيها على علة الخوض في الآيات والطعن فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r16.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r16.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes a conditional construction usually takes the emphatic nun but can omit it; the cited poetic example is cut off in the excerpt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p545/r16.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأما شرط ويلزمها النون الثقيلة في الأغلب وقد لا تلزم كما قال الشاعر:

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.claim: The people addressed are Quraysh, who habitually deny, mock, and attack the signs in their gatherings.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r1.anchor: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء بها والطعن فيها كما هو دأب قريش وديدنهم في أنديتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the people who engage in the signs as the People of the Book, whose habit is similar.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد أهل الكتاب فان ديدنهم ذلك أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r3.claim: The use of idhā signals that this situation is expected to occur, unlike the possible forgetting mentioned later.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r3.anchor: ولذا أتي باذا الدالة على التحقيق وهذا بخلاف النسيان الآتي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r4.claim: Khawḍ originally describes a group entering water; takhāwaḍū is used when they discuss a subject with one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r4.anchor: وأصل الخوض من خاض القوم في الحديث وتخاوضوا إذا تفاوضوا فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r5.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī defines khawḍ as confused, frivolous discussion and play that abandons understanding and clarification.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r5.anchor: الخوض التخليط في المفاوضة على سبيل العبث واللعب وترك التفهم والتبيين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r6.claim: Some investigators derive khawḍ from crossing water and treat its use for discussion as metaphorical; in the Qur'an it is mostly blameworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r6.anchor: أصل معنى الخوض عبور الماء استعير للتفاوض في الأمور وأكثر ماورد في القرآن للذم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r7.claim: Turning away means leaving them and not sitting with them.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r8.claim: Hadīth means speech, and the masculine pronoun refers to God's signs considered as speech; another rationale is considering them as the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r8.anchor: والتذكير باعتبار كونها حديثا فان وصف الحديث بمغايرتها مشير إلى اعتبارها بعنوان الحديثية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r9.claim: The discussion here can mean conversation generally, without restricting it to denial and mockery; some instead gloss it as becoming occupied with another conversation and call the wording parallelism.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بالخوض هنا التفاوض لا بقيد التكذيب والاستهزاء وادعى بعضهم أن المعنى حتى يشتغلوا بحديث غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds it more apparent that the pronoun returns to khawḍ itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r10.anchor: واستظهر عود الضمير إلى الخوض واستدل بعض العلماء بالآية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r11.speaker: بعض العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r11.claim: Some scholars infer from the verse that idhā is iterative, so sitting with the mockers is forbidden whenever they resume their activity; the author says repetition follows from attaching the rule to its occasion, not from idhā itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r11.anchor: ونظر فيه بأن التكرار ليس من إذا بل من ترتب الحكم على مأخذ الاشتقاق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r12.speaker: الحشوية
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r12.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the Ḥashwiyya argument that the verse bans reasoning and debate about God's essence and attributes as a form of engaging the signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r12.anchor: واستدلال بعض الحشوية بها على النهي عن الاستدلال والمناظرة في ذات الله تعالى وصفاته زاعما أن ذلك خوض في آيات الله تعالى مما لا ينبغي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r13.claim: Satan's making the Prophet forget means distracting him from the command to turn away, so he initially sits with them or remains seated; this is hypothetical and did not occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r13.anchor: بأن يشغلك فتنسى الأمر بالاعراض عنهم فتجالسهم ابتداء أو بقاء وهذا على سبيل الفرض إذ لم يقع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Satan has no means of distracting the Messenger of God, which is why the verse uses the conditional in a hypothetical sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r14.anchor: وأنى للشيطان سبيل إلى اشغال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولذا عبر بأن الشرطية المزيدة ما بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r15.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r15.claim: Some investigators say the formal address is to the Prophet while the intended addressee is someone else; another view addresses the listener directly from the outset.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r15.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين أن الخطاب هنا وفيما قبل لسيد المخاطبين عليه الصلاة والسلام والمراد غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r16.speaker: الرافضة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the well-known attribution to the Rāfiḍa is that the Prophet cannot forget, citing the promise that he will not forget; others allow prophetic forgetfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r16.anchor: والمشهور عن الرافضة اختيار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم منزه عن النسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī reports that authoritative Rāfiḍī books forbid prophetic forgetting or inadvertence in revelation, but permit it in other matters if religion is not compromised.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r17.anchor: والذي وقفت عليه في معتبرات كتبهم انهم لا يجوزون النسيان وكذا السهو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r18.claim: Al-Ālūsī excludes forgetfulness arising from Satanic whispers and passing thoughts, considering it impossible for the Messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r18.anchor: وأنا ما أرى أن محل الخلاف النسيان الذي لا يكون منشؤه اشتغال السر بالوساوس والخطرات الشيطانية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r19.speaker: جمهور العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r19.claim: The majority permit prophetic forgetfulness in legal rulings, as the Qur'an and hadith apparently show, but agree that God does not let the Prophet remain uncorrected.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r19.anchor: مذهب جمهور العلماء جواز النسيان عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في احكام الشرع وهو ظاهر القرآن والأحاديث لكن اتفقوا على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لا يقر عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r20.speaker: الأكثرون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r20.claim: Most scholars require God to alert the Prophet immediately and in connection with the event; one group allows the correction to be delayed during his lifetime.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r20.anchor: ثم قال الأكثرون يشترط تنبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام على الفور متصلا بالحادثة ولا يقع فيه تأخير وجوزت طائفة تأخيره مدة حياته

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r21.speaker: أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r21.claim: A group forbids prophetic forgetfulness in acts of delivery and worship, while all agree that forgetfulness in verbal delivery is impossible; al-Isfarāyīnī inclined to this stricter view.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r21.anchor: وإليه مال الاستاذ أبو اسحاق الاسفرائيني

ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r22.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r22.claim: Al-Nawawī validates the first view, which allows forgetfulness when God promptly corrects it, since no harm results and it teaches the rulings for forgetful people.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p182#2/r22.anchor: وصحح النووي الأول فان ذلك لا ينافي النبوة وإذا لم يقر عليه لم يتحصل منه مفسدة ولا ينافي الأمر بالاتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r1.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r1.claim: Al-Qāḍī says most scholars allow inadvertence in the Prophet's non-delivery actions, habits, and inner recollections, while forgetting in verbal revelation and intentional error are unanimously excluded.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r1.anchor: وذكر القاضي أنهم اختلفوا في جواز السهو عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأمور التي لا تتعلق بالبلاغ

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r2.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r2.claim: Some allow a Prophet to forget ordinary speech unrelated to revelation, rulings, or eschatological reports, because they see no resulting harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r2.anchor: وأما السهو في الاقوال الدنيوية وفيما ليس سبيله البلاغ من الكلام الذي لا يتعلق بالاحكام ولا أخبار القيامة وما يتعلق بها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r3.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī holds that prophets cannot err in any report, deliberately or inadvertently, in any state: their words and deeds were closely preserved, and no verbal correction was transmitted, unlike well-known corrections in prayer, the date-poll advice, and the choice of Badr's position.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r3.anchor: وذكر القاضي أنهم اختلفوا في جواز السهو عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأمور التي لا تتعلق بالبلاغ

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r4.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī does not rule out inadvertence in prophets' beliefs about worldly matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r4.anchor: وأما جواز السهو في الاعتقادات في أمور الدنيا فغير ممتنع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī says he will complete this discussion when commenting on the verse about Satan casting into a messenger's wish.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r5.anchor: وسيأتي ان شاء الله تعالى تتمة الكلام على هذا المبحث عند تفسير قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled sīn; nasā here has the causative sense of ansā.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ( ينسينك ) بتشديد السين ونسي بمعنى أنسى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the form nasā is more emphatic than ansā.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : نسي أبلغ من أنسى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r8.claim: In both readings the doubled nūn is the emphatic particle; it is commonly considered necessary after a conditional in accompanied by extra mā, though others deny that it is obligatory, as Ibn Durayd's verse shows.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r8.anchor: والنون في القراءتين مشددة وهي نون التوكيد والمشهور أنها لازمة في الفعل الواقع بعد ان الشرطية المصحوبة بما الزائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r9.speaker: ابن دريد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r9.claim: Ibn Durayd's poetic example is cited for the view that the emphatic nūn need not occur after this conditional construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r9.anchor: وقيل : لا يلزم فيه ذلك وعليه قول ابن دريد : أما ترى رأسي حاكى لونه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r10.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r10.claim: Most commentators understand the reminder as recalling the command to turn away from the mockers.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r10.anchor: أي بعد تذكر الأمر بالاعراض كما عليه جمهور المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r11.claim: Abū Muslim interprets it as after reminding those people by inviting them to the religion and forbidding their engagement with the signs; al-Ālūsī rejects this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p183/r11.anchor: أبو مسلم : المعنى بعد أن تذكرهم بدعائك إياهم إلى الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the reminder as God's reminding the Prophet of the ugliness of sitting with mockers, even if Satan had first made him forget it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r1.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن تكون الذكرى بمعنى تذكير الله تعالى إياه وأن المعنى وإن كان الشيطان ينسيك قبل النهي قبح مجالسة المستهزئين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls this a remote reading grounded in the rationalist doctrine of intrinsic good and evil, which he says learned scholars have demolished; he also denies that such a sitting is universally rejected by reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r2.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه وجه بعيد مبني على قاعدة القبح والحسن التي هدمتها معاول أفكار العلماء الراسخين ثم إنا لا نسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munīr says that if Satan's causing forgetfulness is accepted on transmitted authority, the fitting wording would be wa-in ansāka rather than wa-immā yunsiyannaka; al-Ālūsī calls this another of al-Zamakhsharī's strained interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r3.anchor: وذكر ابن المنير أن اللائق على ما قال وإن أنساك دون وإما ينسينك على أن إنساء الشيطان إن صح

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r4.claim: The explicit noun replaces a pronoun to condemn them as entrenched wrongdoers who put denial and mockery in the place of belief and reverence.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r4.anchor: فوضع المظهر موضع المضمر نعيا عليهم أنهم بذلك الخوض ظالمون واضعون للتكذيب والاستهزاء موضع التصديق والتعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r5.claim: The verse indicates that the forgetful person is not legally responsible while unaware; the issue is discussed under the obligation of the heedless, and al-Ashʿarī has two positions, with non-obligation judged correct because it has no benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r5.anchor: وفي الآية كما قال غير واحد إيذان بعدم تكليف الناسي وهذه المسائل المتنازع فيها بينهم وعنونوها بمسئلة تكليف الغافل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r6.speaker: ابن برهان
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r6.claim: Ibn Burhān transmits that jurists allow obligation of the heedless in the sense that the act remains due, while theologians deny it as inconceivable.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r6.anchor: ونقل ابن برهان في الأوسط عن الفقهاء القول بصحة تكليفه على معنى ثبوت الفعل بالذمة وعن المتكلمين المنع

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the inference that al-Shāfiʿī's rule for a drunk person entails imposing duties on the heedless: drunkenness is a chosen forbidden cause and its penalty differs from mere heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r7.anchor: وقد يظن أن الشافعي لنصه على تكليف السكران يرى تكليف الغافل وهو من بعض الظن فانه إنما كلف السكران عقوبة له

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r8.claim: An objection says that knowing God is required without prior knowledge of the command, forcing the command to precede knowledge and thus burdening someone unaware of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r8.anchor: وأورد على القول بالامتناع أن العبد مكلف بمعرفة الله تعالى بدون العلم بالأمر وذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r9.claim: Replies say general knowledge prevents heedlessness while detailed knowledge is required, or that understanding enough of the address to comply—not believing one is obligated—is the condition; the Minhāj, following al-Ḥāṣil, treats knowledge of God as a consensus exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p184/r9.anchor: بأن المعرفة الاجمالية كافية في انتفاء الغفلة والمكلف به هو المعرفة التفصيلية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r1.claim: Their making sport of God's signs means mocking the Qur'an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r1.anchor: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} يعني: في القرآن بالاستهزاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r2.claim: Turn away from them by leaving them and not sitting with them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r3.speaker: ابن عامر والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads with a fatḥa on nun and doubled sin; the other readers have nun sukun and a light sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر بفتح النون وتشديد السين وقرأ الآخرون بسكون النون وتخفيف السين، {الشيطان}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r4.claim: If someone sat with the mockers forgetfully, he should leave them as soon as he is reminded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p155/r4.anchor: يعني: إذا جلست معهم ناسيا فقهم من عندهم بعدما تذكرت.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r2.claim: Their hostile discourse consists of denying, mocking, and attacking God's signs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r3.claim: Turn away by not sitting with them and by getting up from their company.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r4.claim: The pronoun in 'other discourse' refers to the meaning of the signs, since the signs here are the Qur'an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r4.anchor: أعاد الضمير على معنى الآيات لأنها القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r5.claim: Satan may distract the Prophet through whispering until he forgets the prohibition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r5.anchor: بأن يشغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the verb with a doubled nūn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r7.claim: This means after you remember the prohibition.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r8.claim: The explicit description 'wrongdoers' replaces a pronoun to show that they wronged by substituting denial and mockery for belief and reverence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r8.anchor: فوضع الظاهر موضع المضمر دلالة على أنهم ظلموا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r12.claim: The Muslims said that leaving whenever the Qur'an was mocked would prevent them from sitting and circumambulating in the Sacred Mosque; the verse was then revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:67-69/r12.anchor: أن المسلمين قالوا لئن كنا نقوم كلما استهزءوا بالقرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r3.claim: The Prophet is addressed while the warning is intended for others, making the rebuke more deterrent.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r3.anchor: خاطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد غيره ليكون أردع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r4.claim: To indulge in the signs is to speak without reflection or insight, following desire like someone wading blindly into water and unable to see where error lies.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r4.anchor: بل طوع الهوى , كما يفعل خائض الماء في وضعه لرجله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r5.claim: Turning away means leaving their gathering or doing whatever amounts to ending the association.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r5.anchor: بترك المجالسة أو ما يقوم مقامها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r6.claim: Even their discussion of other matters is treated as rambling, since it contains both trivial and weighty talk without the ordering discipline of religious law.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r6.anchor: أيضا بالخوض , لأن فيه الغث والسمين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r7.claim: The emphatic wording of Satan’s causing forgetfulness stresses that this instruction is important enough not to forget.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r7.anchor: أي إنساء عظيما إشارة إلى أن مثل هذا الأمر جدير بأن لا ينسى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r8.claim: After the reminder, the text names them as wrongdoers rather than using a pronoun, generalizing the warning and identifying darkness as the cause of their conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p652/r8.anchor: على الوصف الذي هو سبب الخوض , وهو الكون في الظلام

BURSEVI:v3p39/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r1.claim: The conditional time clause is governed by its answer, 'turn away'; the address is to the Prophet and his community.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r1.anchor: إذا منصوب بجوابه وهو فأعرض والمراد بالخطاب النبي عليه السلام وأمته

BURSEVI:v3p39/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r2.claim: Khawḍ literally means beginning to engage in something, but conventionally refers to engaging in falsehood; the signs here are the Qur'an.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r2.anchor: والخوض في اللغة الشروع في الشيء مطلقا إلا أنه غلب في الشروع في الشيء الباطل والآيات القرآن

BURSEVI:v3p39/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r3.claim: When Quraysh disbelieve, mock, or attack the Qur'an, leave their gatherings and get up from them.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r3.anchor: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء به والطعن فيه كما هو دأب كفار قريش

BURSEVI:v3p39/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r4.claim: Continue to leave until they discuss something other than God's signs; the pronoun is grammatically masculine because the signs are treated as discourse or Qur'an.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r4.anchor: أي استمر على الإعراض إلى أن يشرعوا في حديث غير آياتنا فالضمير إلى الآيات والتذكير باعتبار كونها حديثا

BURSEVI:v3p39/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r5.claim: Wa-imma derives from in plus the added ma, with the conditional nūn assimilated into it.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r5.anchor: أصله إن ما فأدغمت نون إن الشرطية في ما المزيدة

BURSEVI:v3p39/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r6.claim: What Satan might make the Prophet forget is the instruction to stop sitting with them.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r6.anchor: ما أمرت به من ترك مجالستهم

BURSEVI:v3p39/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r7.claim: After the reminder means after remembering; dhikra is a verbal noun, and the source says no other verbal noun follows this fu'la pattern.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r7.anchor: بعد أن تذكره فهو مصدر بمعنى الذكر

BURSEVI:v3p39/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r8.claim: The wrongdoers are those who put denial and mockery where belief and reverence belong.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r8.anchor: الذين وضعوا التكذيب والاستهزاء موضع التصديق والتعظيم

BURSEVI:v3p39/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r9.claim: The conditional wording makes forgetting a mere possibility, not an event that must have occurred; scholars agree that prophets may experience forgetfulness.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r9.anchor: وهذا الإنساء محض احتمال يدل عليه كلمة إن الشرطية فلا يلزم وقوعه مع أن العلماء قد اتفقوا

BURSEVI:v3p39/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r10.claim: Satan here may mean Iblis or one of his chief troops, since the Prophet's companion had become Muslim and only urged good, unlike the companion of ordinary people.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r10.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان إبليس أو واحد من أكابر جنوده لأن الذي

BURSEVI:v3p39/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r11.claim: A hadith says the Prophet was favored over Adam because his Satan became Muslim with God's help and his wives supported him, whereas Adam's Satan and wife supported his sin.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r11.anchor: كان شيطاني كافرا فأعانني الله عليه فأسلم وكان أزواجي عونا لي

BURSEVI:v3p39/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p39/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p39/r12.claim: Muslims objected that leaving whenever the Qur'an was mocked would prevent them from sitting in the Sacred Mosque and circumambulating the Kaaba; God therefore allowed them to remain to admonish and remind.
BURSEVI:v3p39/r12.anchor: لئن كنا نقوم كلما استهزؤوا بالقرآن لم نستطع

DURR-FULL:v3p290/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p290/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p290/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads this and similar verses as commanding believers to remain united and avoid divisions, since earlier peoples perished through religious disputes and quarrels.
DURR-FULL:v3p290/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} ونحو هذا في القرآن قال: أمر الله المؤمنين بالجماعة

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r1.claim: Qatāda says God forbade sitting with those who deny His signs; if one forgets, one must leave once reminded.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم} قال: نهاه الله أن يجلس مع الذين يخوضون في آيات الله يكذبون بها

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r2.claim: Mujāhid says they mock God's signs; Muḥammad was not to sit with them, and must rise once he remembered the instruction.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} قال: يستهزؤون بها نهى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إن يقعد معهم إلا أن ينسى

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r3.speaker: أبو مالك، سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r3.claim: Abū Mālik and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr identify those who engage in the signs as deniers, specifically the polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r3.anchor: عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} قال: الذين يكذبون بآياتنا يعني المشركين

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r4.speaker: أبو مالك، سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r4.claim: They explain that if one forgets and then remembers, one must not remain seated with the mockers.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r4.anchor: عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} قال: الذين يكذبون بآياتنا يعني المشركين

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says polytheists insulted the Prophet and Qur'an in believers' company, so believers were told to leave until the conversation changed.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r6.anchor: عن السدي في الآية قال: كان المشركون إذا جالسوا المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r7.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r7.claim: Ibn Sīrīn thought the verse was revealed about the people of sectarian innovations and passions.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} قال: كان يرى أن هذه الآية نزلت في أهل الأهواء

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says people of disputation are those who engage in God's signs, and warns against keeping their company.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r8.anchor: عن أبي جعفر قال: لا تجالسوا أهل الخصومات فإنهم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله

DURR-FULL:v3p291/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī identifies followers of religious passions among those who engage in God's signs.
DURR-FULL:v3p291/r9.anchor: عن محمد بن علي قال: أن أصحاب الأهواء من الذين يخوضون في آيات الله

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Meccan polytheists listened to the Prophet and then mocked; the verse directed him to turn away from them.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: كان المشركون يجلسون إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبون أن يسمعوا منه فإذا سمعوا استهزؤوا

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains that when the Prophet rose after mockery, they feared he would leave and warned one another to stop, so they might avoid mockery.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: كان المشركون يجلسون إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبون أن يسمعوا منه

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the mockers as People of the Book and says the Prophet must not sit with them when they speak falsely about the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} قال: هم أهل الكتاب نهى أن يقعد معهم إذا سمعهم يقولون في القرآن غير الحق

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r5.speaker: أبو وائل، إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r5.claim: Abū Wāʾil reports that Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī cited this verse when told that a man told lies to amuse his companions, thereby angering God.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r5.anchor: عن أبي وائل قال: إن الرجل ليتكلم بالكلمة من الكذب ليضحك بها جلساءه فيسخط الله عليه

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r6.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r6.claim: Muqātil says Meccan polytheists mocked the Qur'an when they heard it from the Prophet's companions; believers feared that staying would imply acceptance, so they were told to leave.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل قال: كان المشركون بمكة إذا سمعوا القرآن من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاضوا واستهزؤوا

DURR-FULL:v3p292/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r7.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says this command was abrogated by 4:140, then followed by the command to fight polytheists in 9:5.
DURR-FULL:v3p292/r7.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} الآية قال: نسختها هذه الآية التي في سورة النساء

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God commands believers to remain united and forbids division, explaining that earlier peoples were ruined by religious disputation and quarrels.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، واذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتنا ونحو هذا في القران ، قال : امر الله عز وجل المؤمنين بالجماعة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r2.claim: Al-Suddi, through Abu Malik, glosses discourse in the signs as denial; the same is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r2.anchor: عن السدي عن أبي مالك اذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتناقال : الخوض : التكذيب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r3.speaker: محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r3.claim: Muhammad thought this verse had been revealed concerning people of theological desires.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r3.anchor: عن محمد في هذه الاية : واذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتنا قال : كان يرى ان هذه الاية نزلت في اهل الاهواء

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r4.claim: Al-Suddi, reporting from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, identifies the people to be avoided as polytheists.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r4.anchor: عن السدى ، عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : واذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتنا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says polytheists would attack and mock the Prophet and Quran while sitting with believers, so believers were ordered to leave until the conversation changed.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r5.anchor: عن السدى قوله : واذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتنا فاعرض عنهم قال : كان المشركون اذا جالسوا المؤمنين

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r6.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r6.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi warns that someone who entertains people may incur God's anger; al-Nakha'i affirms this is in scripture and cites the verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1314/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي قال : سمعت أبا وائل يقول : ان الرجل ليجلس المجلس فيحدث جلساءه بأمر ليضحك به القوم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r1.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says God's signs here mean the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : في اياتنا يعني : القران

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies them as People of the Book and says not to sit with them when they speak falsely about the Quran.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : فاعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره قال : هم اهل الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r3.claim: Muqatil explains the command as cutting short one's company with them and not listening until they turn to another subject.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل ، وقوله : واذا رايت الذين يخوضون في اياتنا فاعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره يقول : قصر عن مجالستهم

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r4.speaker: أبو مالك وسعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r4.claim: Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as transmitted by al-Suddi, say that if one forgets and then remembers, one must not continue sitting with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r4.anchor: عن السدى ، عن أبي مالك ، وسعيد بن جبير واما ينسينك الشيطان قال : ان نسيت فذكرت

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r5.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r5.claim: Abu Malik explains after the reminder as after remembering.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r5.anchor: عن السدى ، عن أبي مالك واما ينسينك الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى ، بعد ما تذكر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r6.claim: Muqatil says not to sit with wrongdoers after remembering the prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين يقول : لا تقعد بعدما تذكر النهي

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r7.claim: Muqatil identifies the wrongdoers here as polytheists.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1315/r7.anchor: وبه عن مقاتل قوله : مع القوم الظالمين يعني : المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r1.claim: The command follows the people's denial in 6:66; the switch to a relative clause singles out the especially abusive subset who attack the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { وكذب به قومك } ( الأنعام : 66 ) . والعدول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r2.claim: Most deniers rejected without polemic, but the fiercest group publicly attacked the Qur'an; the Prophet must leave their debate and gatherings until they stop, since shunning all deniers would halt preaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r2.anchor: فأولئك قسم ، والذين يخوضون في الآيات قسم كان أبذى وأقذع ، وأشد كفرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r3.claim: Seeing them means seeing them while they are actively engaged in their polemics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r3.anchor: ومعنى { إذا رأيت الذين يخوضون } إذا رأيتهم في حال خوضهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r4.claim: The relative construction, rather than a bare label or pronoun, explains the unusual withdrawal order: their conduct supplies its rationale and withdrawal lasts until they do its opposite.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r4.anchor: لأن الموصول فيه إيماء إلى وجه الأمر بالإعراض لأنه أمر غريب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r5.claim: The verse is an exemplary case of a relative clause hinting at the cause of an ensuing report or command; its endpoint is the end of the conduct in the clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية أحسن ما يمثل به ، لمجيء الموصول للإيماء إلى إفادة تعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur says the verse supports al-Qutb al-Shirazi's reading of al-Sakkaki: the basis of a statement is its cause; al-Taftazani rejected that interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r6.anchor: صحة ما فسر به القطب الشيرازي في ( شرح المفتاح ) قول السكاكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r7.claim: Khawd literally means entering water on foot rather than swimming, then metaphorically denotes burdensome or difficult action and contrived talk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r7.anchor: والخوض حقيقته الدخول في الماء مشيا بالرجلين دون سباحة ثم استعير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r8.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says Qur'anic usage of khawd is mostly blameworthy initiation; here it means speaking falsely and mockingly about God's signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p288/r8.anchor: قال الراغب : وأكثر ما ورد في القرآن ورد فيما يذم الشروع فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r1.claim: Adding the case of forgetfulness further emphasizes the order to withdraw from the mockers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r1.anchor: عطف حالة النسيان زيادة في تأكيد الأمر بالإعراض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r2.claim: Ascribing forgetfulness to Satan indicates that human constitution gives Satan a share in some natural symptoms; this is not Satan whispering into the Prophet's actions, from which he is protected.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r2.anchor: فدلنا على أن النسيان من آثار الخلقة التي جعل الله فيها حظا العلم الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r3.speaker: جمهور علماء السنة من الأشاعرة وغيرهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r3.claim: The Sunni majority, including Ash'aris, allow prophets to forget in matters other than conveying revelation; Ibn al-Arabi says major Rafidites deny prophetic forgetfulness, and a view is also attributed to some Ash'aris and Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r3.anchor: فالنسيان من الأعراض البشرية الجائزة على الأنبياء في غير تبليغ ما أمروا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r4.claim: Reports say the Prophet once ended a four-rak'ah prayer after two rak'ahs and forgot verses until another man's night recitation reminded him; the source calls these reports authentic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r4.anchor: وقد نسي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسلم من ركعتين في الصلاة الرباعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r5.claim: The Prophet said that he is human and forgets as his followers do, so they should remind him when he forgets; Ibn Ashur calls the hadith authentic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : ( إنما أنا بشر أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r6.claim: The issue is not whether forgetfulness can occur, but how it can be attributed to Satan: God may make some permissible bodily symptoms, like yawning or pleurisy, effects of Satan, while others are assigned to angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r6.anchor: وليس نظرنا في جواز ذلك وإنما نظرنا في إسناد ذلك إلى الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r7.speaker: أيوب عليه السلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r7.claim: Job said that Satan had afflicted him with distress and torment, an example of a bodily trial attributed to Satan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r7.anchor: وقد قال أيوب { أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r8.claim: Permissible human symptoms that neither compromise transmission nor cause sin may be effects of Satan; God protects prophets from Satan in other respects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p290/r8.anchor: الأعراض البشرية الجائزة على الأنبياء التي لا تخل بتبليغ ولا توقع في المعصية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r1.claim: One possible view is that Muhammad alone was protected from every satanic influence, even one causing otherwise permissible human symptoms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قد خص من بين الأنبياء بأن لا سلطة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r2.speaker: جبريل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r2.claim: In the chest-splitting report, Gabriel called what he removed the Prophet's share of Satan, understood as the center of Satan's influence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r2.anchor: أن جبريل لما استخرج العلقة قال : هذا حظ الشيطان منك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r3.claim: In the Muwatta report, the Prophet left Bilal to watch for dawn; Satan kept soothing Bilal like a child until he slept and sunrise came.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r3.anchor: حين نام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ووكل بلالا بأن يكلأ لهم الفجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r4.claim: On this account, the Prophet and the other Muslims slept naturally; only Bilal's sleep was caused by Satan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r4.anchor: فأما نوم النبي والمسلمين عدا بلالا فكان نوما معتادا ليس من عمل الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r5.speaker: عياض
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur says this account is indicated by Qadi Iyad in al-Shifa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا الوجه أشار عياض في ( الشفاء )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet saw the Night of Decree and went to tell people, but two men quarreled and it was lifted; Satan caused their quarrel because he could not lift the night himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r6.anchor: رأى ليلة القدر ، فخرج ليعلم الناس فتلاحى رجلان فرفعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r7.claim: The Prophet is protected from Satanic whispering, but need not be protected from lower effects such as forgetfulness or distraction; whispering produces positive effects while forgetfulness and distraction produce absences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r7.anchor: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم من الوسوسة ، وأما ما دونها مثل الإنساء والنزغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r8.claim: If Satan makes the Prophet forget to withdraw, the command means that once he remembers, he must leave; this forgetfulness redirects him between forms of worship or preaching without sin or Satan achieving misguidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r8.anchor: فالمعنى إن أنساك الشيطان الإعراض عنهم فإن تذكرت فلا تقعد معهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r9.claim: God has lifted accountability for forgetfulness, and the prohibition applies after the Prophet recalls the order to withdraw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r9.anchor: وقد رفع الله المؤاخذة بالنسيان ، ولذلك قال : { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r10.claim: Al-dhikra is a noun meaning recollection, opposite of forgetfulness; the clause describes remembering after an inadvertent lapse and sitting with the mockers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r10.anchor: فالذكرى اسم للتذكر وهو ضد النسيان ، فهي اسم مصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r11.claim: The command to do something entails forbidding its opposite; leaving the gathering after remembrance is the opposite of withdrawing from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291/r11.anchor: وهو ضد فأعرض ، وذلك أن الأمر بالشيء نهي عن ضده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r1.claim: The majority read yunsiyannaka with a vowelless n and an ungeminated s.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { ينسينك } بسكون النون وتخفيف السين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r2.claim: Ibn Amir reads the form with an opened n and geminated s, from the intensive verb tansi'a.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r2.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر بفتح النون وتشديد السين من التنسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r3.claim: Some scholars interpret the address to the Prophet as intended for his community, as in the warning about shirk in 39:65.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r3.anchor: ومن العلماء من تأول هذه الآية بأنها مما خوطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says there is no excuse for applying the community-address interpretation here: unlike shirk in 39:65, forgetfulness is possible for the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن العربي إذا عذرنا أصحابنا في قولهم ذلك في { لئن أشركت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r5.claim: The wrongdoers are the people who polemicize about God's signs; naming them explicitly in place of a pronoun stresses that their polemic is wrongdoing and stubborn denial of truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p291#2/r5.anchor: والقوم الظالمون هم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله ، فهذا من الإظهار في مقام الإضمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a universal mercy and guide whose highest aim is to reform individual, collective, and civilizational affairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r1.anchor: فكان المقصد الأعلى منه صلاح الأحوال الفردية ، والجماعية ، والعمرانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.claim: Individual reform begins with sound belief and includes purification of character, outward worship, and inward virtues such as abandoning envy, rancor, and pride.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r2.anchor: ورأس الأمر فيه صلاح الإعتقاد لأن الإعتقاد مصدر الآداب والتفكير ، ثم صلاح السريرة الخاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.claim: Collective welfare depends on sound individuals and rules governing interaction that restrain competition of desires and impulses; philosophers call this civil politics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r3.anchor: ومن شيء زائد على ذلك وهو ضبط تصرف الناس بعضهم مع بعض على وجه يعصمهم من مزاحمة الشهوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.claim: Civilizational reform preserves order among Muslim communities and regions, serves shared interests, and gives general welfare priority over narrow interests; it is social science.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r4.anchor: حفظ نظام العالم الإسلامي ، وضبط تصرف الجماعات والأقاليم بعضهم مع بعض على وجه يحفظ مصالح الجميع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.claim: The Qur’an explains how to preserve the aims of religion in clear Arabic, and readers are charged to reflect on its verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r5.anchor: وقد أودع ذلك في ألفاظ القرآن التي خاطبنا بها خطابا بينا وتعبدنا بمعرفة مراده والاطلاع عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r6.claim: Some scholars and al-Mashaykhi and al-Sakkaki say God’s full intent can be known, while other Muʿtazilites deny it; the author considers the dispute fruitless, since exhaustive inquiry is required as ability allows even if full knowledge is unattainable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r6.anchor: سواء قلنا إنه يمكن الاطلاع على تمام مراد الله تعالى وهو قول علمائنا والمشائخي والسكاكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r7.claim: God chose Arabic and the Arabs as first bearers of revelation because their language is eloquent, widely accessible, concise yet rich, and their society could receive true perfection without distortion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r7.anchor: وقد اختار الله تعالى أن يكون اللسان العربي مظهرا لوحيه ، ومستودعا لمراده ، وأن يكون العرب هم المتلقين أولا لشرعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r8.claim: Addressing Arabs first does not restrict the law to them: the Qur’an is universal and lasting, though it also initially cleanses and reforms its first Arab audience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r8.anchor: أن ليس المراد من خطاب العرب بالقرآن أن يكون التشريع قاصرا عليهم أو مراعيا لخاصة أحوالهم ، بل إن عموم الشريعة ودوامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r9.claim: Some verses address specifically Arab circumstances, including their lack of prior access to these accounts and their claim revelation would have guided them better than earlier communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r9.anchor: وكان كثير من القرآن مقصودا به خطابهم خاصة ، وإصلاح أحوالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r10.claim: The first of eight principal Qur’anic aims is correcting belief and teaching sound creed, the greatest basis for ethical reform because it removes unsupported submission and false beliefs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r11.claim: A verse ascribes ruin to the people’s idols even though idols do not act; the ruin results from their belief in idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p38#2/r11.anchor: فأسند لآلهتهم زيادة تتبيبهم ، وليس هو من فعل الآلهة ولكنه من آثار الإعتقاد بالآلهة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r1.claim: The address is grammatically singular to the Prophet; some say believers share its intended scope, which Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers because they face the same danger of hearing and being drawn into blasphemous talk.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r1.anchor: لفظ هذا الخطاب مجرد للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده، واختلف في معناه فقيل إن المؤمنين داخلون في الخطاب معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers including believers in the address because the prohibition’s cause—hearing and being drawn into talk against God’s verses—applies equally to them and the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r2.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح، لأن علة النهي وهي سماع الخوض في آيات الله تسلهم وإياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation limits the intended address to the Prophet: his visibly rebuking departure would trouble the polytheists, so he was to leave when they mocked and delved in order to discipline them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل بالمعنى أيضا إنما أريد به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده، لأن قيامه عن المشركين كان يشق عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r4.claim: Khawḍ originally means wading in water and then came to describe plunging into obscure matters by analogy with water’s depths.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r4.anchor: والخوض أصله في الماء ثم يستعمل بعد في غمرات الأشياء التي هي مجاهل تشبيها بغمرات الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r5.claim: Imma is conditional and usually takes the emphatic nūn, though it may occur without it, as a line of poetry illustrates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r5.anchor: وإما شرط وتلزمها النون الثقيلة في الأغلب، وقد لا تلزم كما قال: إما يصبك عدو في مناوأة
