IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAmir alone reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled sīn and open nūn; the meaning is unchanged, but the doubled form is more emphatic.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده «ينسنك» بتشديد السين وفتح النون والمعنى واحد، إلا أن التشديد أكثر مبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r7.claim: Dhikrā and dhikr have the same meaning; the difference is only feminine grammatical form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r7.anchor: والذكرى والذكر واحد في المعنى وإنما هو تأنيث لفظي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r8.claim: Calling them wrongdoers is apt because they put things in the wrong place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r8.anchor: ووصفهم هنا ب الظالمين متمكن لأنهم وضعوا الشيء في غير موضعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r9.claim: Here fa-aʿriḍ means to leave them in a literal, complete withdrawal, as the following prohibition against sitting with them confirms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p303#3/r9.anchor: وفأعرض في هذه الآية بمعنى المفارقة على حقيقة الإعراض وأكمل وجوهه، ويدل على ذلك فلا تقعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r7.claim: Believers should apply this ruling when facing heretics, people of disputation, and those who delve into contentious matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r7.anchor: وينبغي للمؤمن أن يمتثل حكم هذه الآية مع الملحدين وأهل الجدال والخوض فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r8.claim: Al-Tabari reports Abu Jaʿfar’s instruction not to sit with disputants, because they are the people who delve into God’s verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p304/r8.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن أبي جعفر أنه قال لا تجالسوا أهل الخصومات فإنهم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r1.claim: One reported identification of those who dispute the revelations is the polytheists, whose engagement with the Qurʾan consists of denying and mocking it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r1.anchor: أحدها المشركون والثاني اليهود والثالث أصحاب الأهواء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r2.claim: A second identification is the Jews; their disputation resembles the polytheists' denial and mockery.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r2.anchor: والثاني اليهود والثالث أصحاب الأهواء والآيات القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r3.claim: A third identification is people of religious whims, whose disputation takes the form of argument and contentious wrangling.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r4.claim: The revelations being disputed are the Qurʾan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r4.anchor: والآيات القرآن وخوض المشركين فيه تكذيبهم به واستهزاؤهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r5.claim: Leave their company until their talk turns to something other than the Qurʾan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r5.anchor: أي فاترك مجالستهم حتى يكون خوضهم في غير القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads yunsiyannaka with the first nūn open and a doubled sīn and second nūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ينسينك بفتح النون وتشديد السين والنون الثانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r7.claim: The causative form is comparable to garramtuhu and aghramtuhu; the Qurʾan supplies a parallel construction in 86:17.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r7.anchor: وتشديد السين والنون الثانية ومثل هذا غرمته وأغرمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r8.claim: If Satan makes you forget and you sit with them unaware of the prohibition, do not remain after the reminder.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r8.anchor: والمعنى إذا أنساك الشيطان فقعدت معهم ناسيا نهينا لك فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r9.claim: Dhikr and dhikra have the same meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r9.anchor: والذكر والذكرى واحد قال ابن عباس قم إذا ذكرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says to get up once you remember the prohibition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس قم إذا ذكرته والظالمون المشركون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p61#2/r11.claim: The wrongdoers in this verse are the polytheists.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r5.claim: Those who engage in God’s signs are denying and mocking them; one should withdraw until they turn to another topic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r5.anchor: أي: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء {فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r6.claim: The address applies to every member of the community: do not sit with deniers who distort God’s signs; if forgetfulness leads you to sit with them, leave once reminded.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بهذا كل فرد، فرد من آحاد الأمة، ألا يجلس مع المكذبين الذين يحرفون آيات الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r7.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that error, forgetfulness, and coercion have been lifted from his community.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r7.anchor: رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r8.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī, reporting Abū Mālik and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and also Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān explain: if one forgets but then remembers, one must not remain with them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r8.anchor: وقال السدي، عن أبي مالك وسعيد بن جبير في قوله: {وإما ينسينك الشيطان} قال: إن نسيت فذكرت، فلا تجلس معهم. وكذا قال مقاتل بن حيان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr identifies this verse with the instruction in 4:140 not to sit among those who deny or mock God’s revelations, since approving their talk makes one like them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p277#2/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية هي المشار إليها في قوله: {وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب

JISHUMI:v3p2277/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r9.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled nūn; the other readers read it without doubling.
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r9.anchor: قراءة ابن عامر: ينسينك مشددة، والباقون بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v3p2277/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r10.claim: Khawḍ means entering into something while becoming muddied in it; its original sense is walking through water.
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r10.anchor: الخوض: الدخول في الشيء على تلوث به، وأصله المشي في الماء

JISHUMI:v3p2277/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r11.claim: Iʿrāḍ means turning away; ṣadd is a near equivalent and iqbāl its opposite.
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r11.anchor: والإعراض: الذهاب عن الشيء، ونظيره: الصد، ونقيضه: الإقبال

JISHUMI:v3p2277/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r16.claim: It is said the polytheists mocked the Messenger when sitting with believers, so God forbade believers to sit with them.
JISHUMI:v3p2277/r16.anchor: قيل: كان المشركون إذا جالسوا المؤمنين وقعوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r1.claim: The people ridiculing and attacking God’s verses were Quraysh doing so in their meeting places.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r1.anchor: وكانت قريش في أنديتهم يفعلون ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r2.claim: Turn away means do not sit with them and leave their gathering.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r3.claim: Once they move to a different topic, sitting with them is permissible.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r4.claim: The phrase can mean Satan distracts you by whispering until you forget the prohibition on sitting with them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r4.anchor: وإن شغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي عن مجالستهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r5.claim: Alternatively, before the prohibition, Satan may make you forget that reason itself condemns sitting with mockers; the reminder means God warned you of its ugliness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r5.anchor: وإن كان الشيطان ينسينك قبل النهي قبح مجالسة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r9.speaker: المسلمون
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p34/r9.claim: Muslims said that leaving every time the Qur’an was mocked would make it impossible to sit in the Sacred Mosque or circumambulate; a concession was then given.

MUJAHID:v1p217/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p217/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p217/r1.claim: To 'delve into' God's signs means to mock them.
MUJAHID:v1p217/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا ﴾ يقول يستهزئون بآياتنا

MUJAHID:v1p217/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p217/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p217/r2.claim: The Prophet was forbidden to sit with the mockers; if he forgot, he had to leave when reminded.
MUJAHID:v1p217/r2.anchor: فنهى نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقعد معهم إلا أن ينسى فإذا ذكر فليقم وذلك قوله ﴿ فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين ﴾

MUQATIL:6:68-69/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r1.claim: Here “when you see” means “when you hear,” addressed to Muḥammad.
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r1.anchor: { وإذا رأيت } ، يعنى سمعت يا محمد، { الذين يخوضون في آياتنا }

MUQATIL:6:68-69/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r2.claim: Those who dispute God's signs are mocking the Qurʾān and saying false things.
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r2.anchor: يعنى يستهزءون بالقرآن، وقالوا ما لا يصح، قال الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم:

MUQATIL:6:68-69/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r3.claim: Muḥammad is told to leave and not sit with them until their conversation is no longer about God's matter and remembrance.
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r3.anchor: { فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره } ، يعنى فقم عنهم لا تجالسهم حتى يكون حديثهم

MUQATIL:6:68-69/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r4.claim: If Satan makes Muḥammad forget and he sits with them after the prohibition, then once reminded he must not continue sitting.
MUQATIL:6:68-69/r4.anchor: { وإما ينسينك الشيطان } ، يقول: فإن أنساك الشيطان فجالستهم بعد النهى، { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى }

NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r1.claim: The people who dispute God's verses mock and attack the Qur'an; Quraysh did this in their gatherings.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r1.anchor: أى القرآن يعنى يخوضون فى الاستهزاء بها والطعن فيها وكانت قريش فى أنديتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r2.claim: Turn away from them, do not sit with them, and leave their gathering.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ فأعرض عنهم ﴾ ولا تجالسهم وقم عنهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r3.claim: Once they discuss something other than the Qur'an that is permissible, sitting with them is allowed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ حتى يخوضوا فى حديث غيره ﴾ غير القرآن مما يحل فحينئذ يجوز أن تجالسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r4.speaker: شامى
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r4.claim: The Syrian reading yunsiyannaka is from the verb nasiya; nasiya and ansā have the same meaning.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r5.claim: After remembering the prohibition, do not remain with the wrongdoers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p328#5/r5.anchor: بعد أن تذكر ﴿ مع القوم الظالمين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r1.claim: Those who engage in God's signs deny, reject, or mock them.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r2.claim: Though the address explicitly names the Prophet, believers are also included because the cause—hearing mockery of God's signs—applies to them too.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r2.anchor: والخطاب مجرد للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. وقيل: إن المؤمنين داخلون في الخطاب معه. وهو صحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r3.claim: Another view limits the address to the Prophet because his leaving the idolaters would trouble them, whereas the believers' departure would not; the rebuke disciplines them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r3.anchor: وقيل: المراد به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده لأن قيامه عن المشركين كان يشق عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r4.claim: Khawd originally means wading in water, then metaphorically entering obscure matters, likened to the depths of water.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r4.anchor: والخوض أصله في الماء، ثم استعمل بعد في غمرات الأشياء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r5.claim: Another derivation takes khawd from mixing: whatever is mixed has been entered into, as in mixing water with honey.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r6.claim: The Prophet sat with idolaters to admonish and invite them, but they mocked the Qur'an; God ordered a denunciatory withdrawal.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r6.anchor: كان يقعد إلى قوم من المشركين يعظهم ويدعوهم فيستهزءون بالقرآن فأمره الله أن يعرض عنهم إعراض منكر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r7.claim: One who recognizes wrongdoing and knows advice will not be accepted must disapprovingly withdraw and not engage with the wrongdoer.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r7.anchor: إذا علم من الآخر منكرا وعلم أنه لا يقبل منه فعليه أن يعرض عنه إعراض منكر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies them as people who mock God's Book; one must not sit with them unless one forgets, and must leave once reminded.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: «وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا» قال: هم الذين يستهزءون بكتاب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r9.claim: In another report, Mujahid says they are people who say false things about the Qur'an.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r9.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: هم الذين يقولون في القرآن غير الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r10.claim: The verse rebuts those claiming religious authorities and followers may associate with sinners and endorse their views as dissimulation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r10.anchor: في هذه الآية رد من كتاب الله عز وجل على من زعم أن الأئمة الذين هم حجج وأتباعهم لهم أن يخالطوا الفاسقين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r11.claim: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali says not to sit with disputants, identifying them as those who engage in God's signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r11.anchor: عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: لا تجالسوا أهل الخصومات

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi treats the verse as proof that sitting with people who commit major sins is unlawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r12.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهذا دليل على أن مجالسة أهل الكبائر لا تحل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r13.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r13.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad says anyone mocking God's signs must be shunned, believer or unbeliever; his school also forbids assemblies of unbelievers and innovators and hearing or debating them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r13.anchor: قال ابن خويزمنداد: من خاض في آيات الله تركت مجالسته وهجر، مؤمنا كان أو كافرا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r14.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r14.claim: When an innovator asked Ibrahim al-Nakha'i to hear a word, he refused even half a word.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r14.anchor: لأبي عمران النخعي: اسمع مني كلمة فأعرض عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r15.speaker: أيوب السختياني
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r15.claim: A similar refusal to hear an innovator is attributed to Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r15.anchor: ومثله عن أيوب السختياني. وقال الفضيل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r16.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r16.claim: Al-Fudayl says loving an innovator nullifies one's works and removes Islam's light from the heart; marrying one's daughter to one cuts kinship, and sitting with one withholds wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r16.anchor: قال الفضيل بن عياض: من أحب صاحب بدعة أحبط الله عمله وأخرج نور الإسلام من قلبه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r17.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r17.claim: Al-Fudayl hopes God forgives a man if He knows that the man hates an innovator.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68/r17.anchor: وإذا علم الله عز وجل من رجل أنه مبغض لصاحب بدعة رجوت أن يغفر الله له

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r1.claim: Al-Hakim transmits from Aisha that the Prophet said honoring an innovator helps demolish Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r1.anchor: روى أبو عبد الله الحاكم عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r2.claim: These proofs invalidate the claim that sitting with innovators is permissible if one guards one's hearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r2.anchor: فبطل بهذا كله قول من زعم أن مجالستهم جائزة إذا صانوا أسماعهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r3.claim: The conditional particle ima generally requires the emphatic nūn, though it may omit it, as an unnamed poet's line demonstrates.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r3.anchor: «إما» شرط، فيلزمها النون الثقيلة في الأغلب وقد لا تلزم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Amir read yunsiyannaka with doubled sīn for intensification; nasiya and ansā are two forms with the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن عامر «ينسينك» بتشديد السين على التكثير

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r5.claim: An uncredited poetic line beginning “Salma said” illustrates ansā; a second line is attributed to Imru al-Qays.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r5.anchor: قالت سليمى أتسري اليوم أم تقل وقد ينسيك بعض الحاجة الكسل

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r6.claim: If Satan makes you forget to leave the mockers and you sit after the prohibition, leave once reminded; the wrongdoers are idolaters.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r6.anchor: المعنى: يا محمد إن أنساك الشيطان أن تقوم عنهم فجالستهم بعد النهي

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r7.claim: Al-dhikrā is the noun for reminding.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r8.claim: The wrongdoers named at the end of the verse are the polytheists.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r9.claim: One view addresses the Prophet but intends his community to exonerate him from forgetfulness; another says it specifically addresses him because forgetfulness is possible for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r9.anchor: قيل: هذا خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته ذهبوا إلى تبرئته عليه السلام من النسيان

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the community-as-recipient explanation used for 39:65 cannot excuse this verse, since prophetic forgetfulness is possible.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وإن عذرنا أصحابنا في قولهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r11.claim: The Prophet said Adam forgot and his descendants forgot; al-Tirmidhi transmitted and graded the report sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r11.anchor: قال عليه السلام: " نسي آدم فنسيت ذريته "

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r12.claim: The Prophet said he is human and forgets as others do, asking them to remind him; the report is in the Sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r12.anchor: إنما أنا بشر مثلكم أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r13.claim: After hearing a man's recitation, the Prophet said it had reminded him of a verse he had forgotten.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r13.anchor: لقد أذكرني آية كذا وكذا كنت أنسيتها

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r14.speaker: عامة العلماء والأئمة النظار
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r14.claim: Most scholars and theologians, as reported by Qadi Iyad, allow prophetic forgetfulness in actions and rulings conveying law, provided God alerts him and does not leave him in error.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r14.anchor: ذهب إلى الأول فيما ذكره القاضي عياض عامة العلماء والأئمة النظار

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r15.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر وأكثر العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r15.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr and most scholars require God's alert to come immediately with the event.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r15.anchor: وهو مذهب القاضي أبي بكر والأكثر من العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r16.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r16.claim: Abu al-Ma'ali allows God's alert to be delayed, provided it comes before the Prophet's life and transmission end.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r16.anchor: ما لم ينخرم عمره وينقطع تبليغه، وإليه نحا أبو المعالي

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r17.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r17.claim: A group including Abu Ishaq denies prophetic forgetfulness in acts conveying religion and ritual acts, and unanimously denies it in conveyed statements; they reinterpret apparent reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r17.anchor: ومنعت طائفة من العلماء السهو عليه في الأفعال البلاغية والعبادات الشرعية

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r18.speaker: الباطنية وطائفة من أرباب علم القلوب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r18.claim: The Batinites and some esoteric spiritual authorities say the Prophet does not forget, but deliberately presents an appearance of forgetting to establish a practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r18.anchor: وشذت الباطنية وطائفة من أرباب علم القلوب فقالوا: لا يجوز النسيان عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r19.claim: The author rejects Abu al-Muzaffar al-Isfarayini's view as unsound because deliberate forgetting and not forgetting are opposites that cannot be combined.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:68#2/r19.anchor: وهو منحى غير سديد، وجمع الضد مع الضد مستحيل بعيد

QASHANI:6:66-68/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:66-68/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:66-68/r5.claim: Engaging in God’s signs means projecting the self’s qualities and affirming its own knowledge and power; such people are veiled and associators.
QASHANI:6:66-68/r5.anchor: صفاتنا بإظهار صفات نفوسهم وإثبات العلم والقدرة

QASHANI:6:66-68/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:66-68/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:66-68/r6.claim: One should turn away because they are veiled and associate others with God.
QASHANI:6:66-68/r6.anchor: لا { فأعرض عنهم } فإنهم محجوبون مشركون

QASHANI:6:66-68/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:66-68/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:66-68/r7.claim: Satan’s distraction comes through seductive falsehoods and the self’s whispering; displaying one’s own qualities makes one resemble them and incline toward their company.
QASHANI:6:66-68/r7.anchor: وسوسة نفسك فتظهر ببعض صفاتها وتجانسهم بذلك فتميل إلى صحبتهم

QASHANI:6:66-68/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:66-68/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:66-68/r8.claim: After God reminds him, the Prophet must not sit with those who place their own qualities where God’s qualities belong and veil the divine with themselves.
QASHANI:6:66-68/r8.anchor: الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بوضع صفاتهم موضع صفاتي وحجبوها بصفاتهم

QASHANI:6:66-68/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:66-68/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:66-68/r9.claim: Their company can itself cause a temporary shift into veiling, so the warning protects against the harm of companionship.
QASHANI:6:66-68/r9.anchor: فإن صحبتهم تؤثر فيوشك أن تقع في الاحتجاب بشؤم صحبتهم على سبيل التلوين

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r1.claim: The previous verse says the Messenger need not stay with deniers; this verse adds that when they mock the religion and attack the Messenger, believers must avoid their company.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r1.anchor: الذين يكذبون بهذا الدين فإنه لا يجب على الرسول أن يلازمهم وأن يكون حفيظا عليهم ثم بين في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r2.claim: One view takes the address as directed to the Prophet, with others intended by the command.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r2.anchor: قيل إنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد غيره

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r3.claim: Another view addresses someone other than the Prophet, namely any listener who sees people mocking the signs.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لغيره أي إذا رأيت أيها السامع الذين يخوضون في آياتنا

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that polytheists insulted and mocked the Prophet and Qur’an when sitting with believers, so they were ordered to leave until the subject changed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r4.anchor: ونقل الواحدي أن المشركين كانوا إذا جالسوا المؤمنين وقعوا في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r5.claim: Khawḍ means engaging in conversation frivolously or playfully; saying people were left khāʾiḍūn implies they had started saying things that should not be said.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r5.anchor: ولفظ الخوض في اللغة عبارة عن المفاوضة على وجه العبث واللعب ، قال تعالى حكاية عن الكفار : { وكنا نخوض مع الخائضين }

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r6.speaker: الحشوية
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r6.claim: The Ḥashwiyya use this verse to prohibit theological reasoning and debate about God’s essence and attributes, calling it forbidden engagement with His signs.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r6.anchor: ومن الحشوية من تمسك بهذه الآية في النهي عن الاستدلال والمناظرة في ذات الله تعالى وصفاته

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects that argument: exegetes and the language use khawḍ here for entering into the signs to attack or mock them, not reasoned theological debate.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r7.anchor: أنا نقلنا عن المفسرين أن المراد من ( الخوض ) الشروع في آيات الله تعالى على سبيل الطعن والاستهزاء

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled nūn; form II and form IV can function alike, as in the example from 74:17.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r8.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { ينسينك } بالتشديد وفعل وأفعل يجريان مجرى واحد كما بينا ذلك في مواضع

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r9.claim: Rāzī prefers the common reading because 18:63 uses the related form in saying that Satan made the speaker forget.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r9.anchor: والاختيار قراءة العامة لقوله تعالى : { وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان } ( الكهف : 63 )

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r10.claim: If you forget and remain seated, do not stay after being reminded; get up once you remember.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r10.anchor: ومعنى الآية : إن نسيت وقعدت فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى ، وقم إذا ذكرت

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r11.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r11.claim: Al-Layth says dhikrā is a noun meaning reminder.

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r12.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says dhikrā can mean remembrance or mention.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء : الذكرى يكون بمعنى الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r13.claim: The wrongdoers in this passage are the polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v13p21#2/r13.anchor: وقوله : { مع القوم الظالمين } يعني مع المشركين

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r1.claim: Because the verse then forbids sitting after the reminder, turning away means physically rising and leaving their company.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r1.anchor: صار ذلك دليلا على أن المراد أن يعرض عنهم بالقيام من عندهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r2.speaker: الذين يتمسكوا بظواهر الألفاظ
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r2.claim: Those committed to the wording's apparent sense do not allow a form of disengagement other than leaving them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r2.anchor: الذين يتمسكوا بظواهر الألفاظ ويزعمون وجوب إجرائها على ظواهرها لا يجوزون ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r3.speaker: الذين يقولون المعنى هو المعتبر
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r3.claim: Those who prioritize meaning allow any action that achieves the intended public display of disapproval.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r3.anchor: المعنى هو المعتبر جوزوا ذلك قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r4.claim: Even if the Messenger fears leaving, he must perform the obligation; excusing him would undermine confidence in the duties he conveyed.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r4.anchor: كل ما أوجب على الرسول فعله وجب عليه ذلك سواء ظهر أثر الخوف أو لم يظهر

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r5.claim: For someone other than the Messenger, severe fear may remove the duty to leave because failure does not create the same threat to trust in revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r5.anchor: أما غير الرسول فإنه عند شدة الخوف قد يسقط عنه الفرض

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r6.claim: The instruction not to remain after remembering indicates that legal responsibility is lifted from a person who forgets.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r6.anchor: يفيد أن التكليف ساقط عن الناسي

RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r7.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r7.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues that if ignorance excuses, inability does so more strongly; impossible duties are not imposed, capacity precedes action, and unbelievers therefore cannot be commanded to believe.
RAZI-FULL:v13p22/r7.anchor: قال الجبائي : إذا كان عدم العلم بالشيء

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r1.claim: The Messenger's duty is to convey the message; realizing connection through divine existence and state belongs to God's power and eternal will.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r1.anchor: يعني قل لهم إنما على تبليغ الرسالة ، فأما تحقيق الوصلة بالوجود والحال

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r2.claim: Do not join those disputing God's signs or answer expansively; turn away graciously and do not listen to their incoherent talk.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r2.anchor: لا توافقهم في الحالة ، ولا ترد عليهم ببسط القالة . ذرهم ووحشتهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r3.claim: If forgetfulness occurs, recover through remembrance and alertness, then avoid repeating the mistake and suffering painful punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r3.anchor: فتداركته بحسن التذكر وجميل التنبه ، فاجتهد ألا ( تزل )

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r4.claim: Those unstained by wrongdoing will be kept apart on Resurrection Day from the pains prepared for wrongdoers.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r4.anchor: أي من كان نقي ( الثوب ) عن ارتكاب الإجرام يعزل يوم نشره

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r5.claim: God has prepared hidden stratagems that will break wrongdoers' veil of delusion and hardness when He brings them upon them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r5.anchor: فإنا أعتدنا لهم ( من خفي المكر ما إذا أحللناه بهم كسرنا عليهم ) خمار الوهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r6.claim: When disbelievers invite Muslims back to shirk, guidance and clear proof cannot rationally be traded for error or Paradise abandoned for Hell.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r6.anchor: أنؤثر الضلال على الهدى بعد طلوع شمس البرهان ؟ وندع الطريقة المثلى

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r7.claim: Someone delivered from Satan's companions and able to see their error would not follow them back into their company.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r7.anchor: وكيف يساعد أتباع الشيطان من وجد الخلاص من صحبتهم ، وأبصر الغي

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r8.claim: The realized should remain in intimate communion; a tongue accustomed to whispering with the Sovereign will not turn to address the lowly.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r8.anchor: أمرنا بملازمة محل المناجاة لأن اللسان إن تعود نجوى السلطان

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r9.claim: No newly arising purpose can obstruct God's power, and His judgment does not fall short in governing any existent thing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r9.anchor: لا يعترض على قدرته - سبحانه - حدوث مقصود ، ولا يتقاصر حكمه

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r1.claim: The disbelievers’ vain discussion of God’s signs aims to deny and deride them.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r1.anchor: The disbelievers engage in vain discussion about the signs of God, seeking to deny and deride them

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r2.claim: The Quran associates vain discussion with pejorative play, warns against taking religion as play or diversion, and commands avoidance of vain talk generally.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r2.anchor: The Quran links such vain discussion elsewhere with “playing” in a pejorative sense

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r3.claim: Religious and legal gossip can damage the community: false adultery accusations may cause miscarriages of justice, division, and mistrust.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r3.anchor: 24:14–16 indicates that vain discussion in matters of religion and law can have serious consequences for the community

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r4.claim: The counsel addresses the Prophet and all believers: withdraw from religious disparagement until the topic changes; other verses reinforce this.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r4.anchor: This verse thus counsels the Prophet, and by extension all believers, to avoid or remove themselves from groups engaged in vain discussion about religious matters

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r5.claim: One need only leave until the group moves to another topic.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r5.anchor: Here, one need only turn away from them until they move on to another topic

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r6.speaker: some reports
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r6.claim: Some reports connect the warning with 6:65’s factions, extending it to believers in fruitless, divisive religious debate.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r6.anchor: Some reports connect the warning in this verse regarding those

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r7.speaker: some literalists
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r7.claim: Some literalists read this as forbidding all religious discussion and debate and requiring reliance only on literal scripture.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r7.anchor: Some literalists have taken this verse to mean a prohibition against all discussion and debate regarding religious issues

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that reading: yakhūḍū means disrespectful, disparaging discussion, not sincere religious deliberation, which the Quran encourages.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r8.anchor: But al-Rāzī rejects such an interpretation

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r9.claim: Satan may cause forgetfulness or make people miss when talk turns disparaging; once aware, they should leave.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r9.anchor: Satan may cause people to forget the prohibition against sitting among those engaged in vain discussion of religion

STUDYQURAN:6:68/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r10.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r10.claim: That Satan can cause the Prophet to forget raises difficult issues, though other verses indicate prophets can be subject to Satan’s whisperings.
STUDYQURAN:6:68/r10.anchor: that he is capable of causing the Prophet to forget raises some difficult issues (Āl)

TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r1.claim: The polytheists' engagement with the revealed signs means mocking them, insulting their messenger, and denying them; turn away until they discuss something else, and leave if you remember after forgetting. Their wrongdoing is this improper mockery.
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r1.anchor: فصد عنهم بوجهك، وقم عنهم، ولا تجلس معهم، {حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره} [النساء: 140]

TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r2.claim: Qatada says God forbade sitting with people who deny His signs, and if one forgets, he must leave once he remembers.
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون} [الأنعام: 68] في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره

TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r3.speaker: أبو مالك، سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r3.claim: In a report transmitted by al-Suddi, Abu Malik and Saʿid ibn Jubayr say these are people who deny God's signs.
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي مالك، وسعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} [الأنعام: 68]

TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says that polytheists would sit with believers, curse the Prophet and Qur'an, and mock them, so God ordered the believers to leave until the conversation changed.
TAB-FULL:v9p312#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره وإما ينسينك الشيطان

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r1.claim: Mujahid explains engaging in God's signs as denying them.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {يخوضون في آياتنا} [الأنعام: 68] قال: «يكذبون بآياتنا»

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar warns believers not to sit with people given to religious disputation, identifying them as those who engage in God's signs.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، قال: «لا تجالسوا أهل الخصومات، فإنهم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله»

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas links this verse with 6:159, 3:105, and 42:13: God commands believers to unite and forbids division and disagreement, through which earlier peoples perished in religious disputation.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r3.anchor: أمر الله المؤمنين بالجماعة، ونهاهم عن الاختلاف والفرقة، وأخبرهم أنه إنما هلك من كان قبلهم

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r4.claim: Mujahid says the people mock the signs and that the Prophet must leave their company when he remembers the ban, even if he had forgotten it.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا} [الأنعام: 68] قال: يستهزئون بها

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports the occasion: polytheists came to hear the Prophet, then mocked after hearing him, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r5.anchor: قال ابن جريج: كان المشركون يجلسون إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبون أن يسمعوا منه، فإذا سمعوا استهزءوا

TAB-FULL:v9p315/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r6.speaker: أبو مالك، السدي
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r6.claim: Al-Suddi, transmitting from Abu Malik, identifies the people as polytheists and says that after remembering, one must not remain seated with them.
TAB-FULL:v9p315/r6.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي مالك، قوله: {وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا فأعرض عنهم

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib defines khawḍ as entering and moving through water, metaphorically used for entering into affairs; Qurʾānic usage is mostly blameworthy.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r4.anchor: ذكر الراغب في المفردات أن الخوض هو الشروع في الماء والمرور فيه

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r5.claim: Here khawḍ means entering into false talk and persisting in it, such as discussing God’s true signs mockingly and at length.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r5.anchor: وهو الدخول في باطل الحديث والتوغل فيه كذكر الآيات الحقة والاستهزاء بها

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r6.claim: Turning away means not joining their talk, for example by standing up and leaving or otherwise making clear one is not participating.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r6.anchor: والمراد بالإعراض عدم مشاركتهم فيما يخوضون فيه كالقيام عنهم والخروج من بينهم

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r7.claim: The restriction lasts only while they mock or discuss the signs; it does not forbid every gathering or sitting with them for a sound purpose.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r7.anchor: وتقييد النهي بقوله { حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره } للدلالة على أن المنهي عنه ليس مطلق مجالستهم

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r8.claim: The wording omits a repeated clause equivalent to those who engage in the signs’ mockery, relying on the relative clause to avoid repetition.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الكلام نوعا من إيجاز الحذف فإن تقدير الكلام وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا يخوضون فيها

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r9.claim: Though given in an argument against polytheists, the rule’s underlying rationale extends to anyone who mocks God’s signs.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r9.anchor: والكلام وإن وقع في سياق الاحتجاج على المشركين لكن ما أشير إليه من الملاك يعممه فيشمل غيرهم

TABATABAI:6:67-68/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r10.claim: The verse calls those who mock the signs unjust and prohibits sharing in their wrongdoing; 4:140 similarly says that sitting with them would make one like them.
TABATABAI:6:67-68/r10.anchor: فالخوض في آيات الله ظلم والآية إنما نهت عن مشاركة الظالمين في ظلمهم، وقد ورد في مورد آخر من كلامه تعالى

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r1.claim: The verse requires withdrawal from mockers only while they are engaged in mocking, not permanent avoidance; “other talk” is the discourse about the signs that they had been pursuing.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r1.anchor: فقد تبين أن الآية لا تأمر بالإعراض عن الخائضين في آيات الله تعالى بل إنما تأمر بالإعراض عنهم

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r2.claim: The pronoun in ghayrihi refers to the discourse about God’s signs in which they were engaged, understood as the activity prohibited in the verse.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r2.anchor: والضمير في قوله { غيره } راجع إلى الحديث الذي يخاض فيه في آيات الله باعتبار أنه خوض

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r3.claim: In imma yunsiyannaka, mā is an added particle for emphasis or mitigation, the nūn marks emphasis, and the underlying form is wa-in yunsik.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r3.anchor: في قوله { إما ينسينك } زائد يفيد نوعا من التأكيد أو التقليل، والنون للتأكيد

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r4.claim: The wording intensifies the prohibition: even if Satan causes forgetfulness, once reminded one must leave promptly, since the pious cannot share in mockers’ activity.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r4.anchor: والكلام في مقام التأكيد والتشديد للنهي أي حتى لو غفلت عن نهينا بما أنساكه الشيطان ثم ذكرت فلا تهاون

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r5.claim: The Prophet is addressed, but the intended addressees are other members of the community; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī’s prior account of prophetic impeccability rules out a prophet forgetting a divine rule and acting against it in a way others could cite.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r5.anchor: والخطاب في الآية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمقصود غيره من الأمة فقد تقدم في البحث عن عصمة الأنبياء

TABATABAI:6:68-69/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r6.claim: The later Medinan instruction in 4:140 repeats the earlier Meccan rule of 6:68 and addresses believers, supporting the view that the Prophet is the grammatical addressee while others are intended.
TABATABAI:6:68-69/r6.anchor: فإن المراد في الآية وهي مدنية بالحكم الذي نزل في الكتاب هو ما في هذه الآية من سورة الأنعام وهي مكية

TABRISI:6:68-69/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:6:68-69/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled sīn; doubling the medial consonant can causativize a verb, as in ʿazzamtu beside aʿzamtu.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحده ينسينك بالتشديد والباقون ينسينك بالتخفيف

TABRISI:6:68-69/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:6:68-69/r2.claim: The other readers use the lighter form, supported by the wording of 18:63.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r2.anchor: حجة من خفف قوله وما أنسانية إلا الشيطان

TABRISI:6:68-69/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r3.claim: Dhikrā may be accusative as an implied command to remind them, or nominative as a predicate or subject in “a reminder is upon you,” as in 42:48.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r3.anchor: ذكرى يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب على معنى ولكن ذكروهم ذكرى ويجوز أن يكون

TABRISI:6:68-69/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:6:68-69/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says Muslims asked how they could leave whenever polytheists mocked the Qur’an, since that would bar them from the Sacred Mosque and circling the House; verse 6:69 then ordered them to remind and teach mockers as far as possible.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ع: لما نزلت { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى مع القوم الظالمين } قال المسلمون كيف نصنع

TABRISI:6:68-69/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r5.claim: The address is to the Prophet and the people wading in the signs are unbelievers; another view takes the address to him while intending someone else.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r5.anchor: خاطب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي إذا رأيت هؤلاء الكفار. وقيل: الخطاب له والمراد غيره

TABRISI:6:68-69/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r6.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:6:68-69/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Saʿid ibn Jubayr explain their wading as denying God’s signs and religion; the word also suggests confused, frivolous discussion without understanding or clarification.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r6.anchor: ومعنى يخوضون يكذبون بآياتنا وديننا عن الحسن وسعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:6:68-69/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r7.claim: Turn away from them by leaving and not sitting with them until they discuss something other than mockery of the Qur’an.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r7.anchor: { فأعرض عنهم } أي فاتركهم ولا تجالسهم { حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره }

TABRISI:6:68-69/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r8.claim: The command prevents futile argument with people in that state, which would put proof in the wrong place and diminish explanation and debate.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r8.anchor: لأن من حاج من هذه حاله فقد وضع الشيء غير موضعه وحط من قدر البيان والحجاج

TABRISI:6:68-69/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r9.claim: The phrase means: if Satan makes you forget Our prohibition against sitting with them.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r9.anchor: المعنى وإن أنساك الشيطان نهينا إياك عن الجلوس معهم

TABRISI:6:68-69/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69/r10.claim: Although forgetfulness is God’s act, it is attributed to Satan because it follows neglected thought and accumulating Satanic whispers; by analogy, death is attributed to one who exposes another to fatal cold.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r10.anchor: والجواب إنما أضافه إلى الشيطان لأن تعالى أجرى العادة بفعل النسيان عند الإعراض عن الفكر

TABRISI:6:68-69/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r11.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:68-69/r11.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says “after the reminder” means after remembering God’s prohibition and the duty to withdraw.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r11.anchor: أي بعد ذكرك نهينا وما يجب عليك من الإعراض عن الجبائي

TABRISI:6:68-69/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:6:68-69/r12.claim: Abu Muslim says it means after reminding them by inviting them to faith, so withdraw in despair and remind them while hope remains.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه بعد أن تذكرهم بدعائك إياهم إلى الدين عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:6:68-69/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي
TABRISI:6:68-69/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi identify the wrongdoers as gatherings of disbelievers and immoral people who openly deny and mock revelation.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r13.anchor: { مع القوم الظالمين } يعني في مجالس الكفار والفساق الذي يظهرون التكذيب بالقرآن

TABRISI:6:68-69/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69/r14.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:6:68-69/r14.claim: Al-Balkhi selects the view that the prohibition applied in early Islam, when Muslims were few, and was later abrogated by 4:140.
TABRISI:6:68-69/r14.anchor: واختاره البلخي وقال كان ذلك في أول الإسلام وكثر المسلمون

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r1.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r1.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi argues that the verse refutes the Imami permission of taqiyya for prophets and imams and denies that prophets can forget.
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r1.anchor: قال الجبائي: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على بطلان قول الإمامية في جواز التقية على الأنبياء

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabrisi replies that Imamis allow an imam’s taqiyya only on matters supported by decisive proof that leaves the duty clear, never on rulings known only through the imam without other evidence.
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r2.anchor: لأن الإمامية إنما تجوز التقية على الإمام فيما تكون عليه دلالة قاطعة توصل إلى العلم

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r3.claim: A prophet who has already explained a legal matter may omit explaining it again when circumstances call for that; the report about ʿUmar’s question on kalāla illustrates this.
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r3.anchor: كما إذا تقدم من النبي بيان في شيء من الأشياء الشرعية فإنه يجوز منه أن لا يبين

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r4.claim: A report says ʿUmar asked the Prophet about kalāla and was told, “The sword verse suffices for you.”
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r4.anchor: ألا ترى إلى ما روي أن عمر بن الخطاب سأله عن الكلالة فقال: " يكفيك آية السيف

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r5.claim: Imamis forbid prophets and imams from forgetfulness in conveying revelation, but allow lapses in other matters if reason remains intact; sleep and fainting are likewise permitted and resemble lapses.
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r5.anchor: وأما النسيان والسهو فلم يجوزوهما عليهم فيما يؤدونه عن الله تعالى فأما ما سواه فقد جوزوا

TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabrisi calls al-Jubbaʾi’s accusation a mistaken conjecture, adding that some suspicion is sinful.
TABRISI:6:68-69#2/r6.anchor: فهذا ظن منه فساد وإن بعض الظن إثم

THALABI:v4p157/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p157/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p157/r1.claim: Here, disputing the signs means mocking and lying about the Quran.
THALABI:v4p157/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن الاستهزاء والكذب فأعرض عنهم فاتركهم ولا تجالسهم

THALABI:v4p157/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p157/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p157/r2.claim: Believers must leave the mockers and not sit with them until they turn to another subject.
THALABI:v4p157/r2.anchor: فأعرض عنهم فاتركهم ولا تجالسهم حتى يخوضوا يدخلوا في حديث غيره

THALABI:v4p157/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p157/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p157/r3.claim: Polytheists insulted the Prophet and mocked the Quran when seated with believers, so God forbade believers to sit with them.
THALABI:v4p157/r3.anchor: وذلك إن المشركين كانوا إذا جالسوا المؤمنين وقعوا في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسبوا واستهزؤا بالقرآن،

THALABI:v4p157/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p157/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عامر
THALABI:v4p157/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Amir read yunsūnaka with a doubled nūn.
THALABI:v4p157/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن عباس وابن عامر: ينسونك بالتشديد الشيطان فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والسدي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r1.claim: The polytheists insulted the Messenger and Qur'an, abused and mocked them in believers' company, so believers were told to leave until the talk changed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r1.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس (¬5) وسعيد بن جبير والسدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the forbidden discourse as denying the Qur'an and the Prophet and mocking them, and says to leave until they discuss something else.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أمر الله رسوله فقال: إذا رأيت المشركين يكذبون بالقرآن وبك ويستهزئون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r3.claim: They gloss the people’s delving into God's signs as denial and mockery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r3.anchor: ومعنى: {يخوضون في آياتنا} أي: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r4.speaker: ابن عامر والعامة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r4.claim: Ibn Amir reads yunsiyannaka with a doubled consonant; the general reading is preferred, supported by the wording in 18:63.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r5.claim: The causative forms faʿʿala and afʿala can function alike, as in the parallel wording of 86:17.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r5.anchor: وفعل وأفعل يجريان مجرى واحدا كما بينا ذلك في مواضع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r6.claim: If the Prophet forgets and remains seated, he should get up as soon as he remembers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: إن نسيت فقعدت {فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r7.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r7.claim: Al-Layth defines dhikrā as a noun meaning reminder.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r8.claim: Al-Farra says dhikrā can mean dhikr or admonition, citing the wording "wa-lākin dhikrā" in the following verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p209/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء: (الذكرى يكون بمعنى: الذكر، كقوله تعالى: {فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r1.claim: He directs readers to the discussion of dhikrā at the verse in Hud about its being a reminder for those who remember.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the wrongdoers in this command as the polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p211/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {مع القوم الظالمين} قال ابن عباس: (يعني: المشركين)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p155/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p155/r1.claim: Kh waḍ in God's signs means speaking of them mockingly.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r1.claim: Their disputatious talk means denying and mocking God’s signs.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r2.claim: When polytheists deny the Quran and the Prophet and mock them, the Messenger must leave their company.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r2.anchor: أمر الله تعالى رسوله عليه السلام فقال: إذا رأيت المشركين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r3.claim: They may be joined again when their discussion turns to something other than the Quran.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r3.anchor: حتى يكون خوضهم في غير القرآن { وإما ينسينك الشيطان }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r4.claim: If one forgets and stays seated, one should leave as soon as one remembers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:68-69/r4.anchor: إن نسيت فقعدت { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى } فقم إذا ذكرت

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r1.claim: Havḍ means plunging into a matter in an amusement-like and excessive manner.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r1.anchor: “Havd”, eğlence tarzında ve aşırı derecede dalmak demektir.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r2.claim: He links the instruction to 4:140, whose parallel wording clarifies the general address and the meanings of plunging into the verses and turning away.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r2.anchor: âyeti de (bak) bunun tefsîri olduğundan hitâbın hitâb-ı âm olduğunu, “havd”ın ve “i‘râz”ın mânalarını vâzıhan göstermiştir.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r3.speaker: Haşviyye
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r3.claim: Elmalılı rejects the Hashwiyya inference that the verse forbids deep inquiry into theology, argument from evidence, or debate.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r3.anchor: bazı Haşviyye’nin tevehhüm ettiği gibi bundan ilâhiyat mesâilinde ta‘mîk u tetebbu‘un, istidlâl ve münazaranın âyâtullaha dalmaktır diye hurmetini istinbâta kalkışmamalı

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r4.claim: Even during argument over proof, one should not become so absorbed that one neglects the matter the proof establishes.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r4.anchor: ancak delil ile uğraşırken medlulden tegāfül edecek derecede dalgınlığa da düşmemelidir.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r5.claim: The mockers and deniers in view include the Meccan Quraysh polytheists.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r5.anchor: ki Mekke’de Kureyş müşrikleri böyle yapıyorlardı

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r6.claim: When people exceed bounds by mocking, taunting, denying, or ridiculing the revelations, the believer should withdraw and not sit with them.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r7.speaker: İbn Âmir
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r7.claim: Ibn Amir reads the verb in the tafʿīl form; Elmalılı glosses the possibility as Satan occupying the addressee and causing the prohibition to be forgotten.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r8.claim: The possibility of being made to forget reflects that the address applies generally to every believer; Satan may distract someone until he forgets the instruction.

ELMALILI:6:68-69/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r9.claim: Once reminded, one must not remain seated with the wrongdoers; their label signals transgression in the meaning of havḍ and extends the prohibition to sitting with wrongdoers generally.
ELMALILI:6:68-69/r9.anchor: “Zâlimîn” tâbir olunması “havd” mefhûmunda haddini tecavüz mânası bulunduğunu iş‘âr ve illet-i nehyi ta‘mîm ile ale’l-umûm zâlimlerle beraber oturmanın dahi menhî olduğunu tasrihtir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r1.claim: Diving into God’s signs means mocking the Qur’an or attempting to discredit it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r1.anchor: “Allah’ın âyetleri hakkında ileri-geri konuşmaya dalmak”tan maksat, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’i alaya almak veya eleştirmeye kalkışmaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r2.claim: If one cannot stop the mockery, one must leave until the group changes the subject; the instruction is repeated at 4:140.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r2.anchor: Âyet, bu şekilde davrananların –eğer engel olmak mümkün değilse– başka bir konuya geçinceye kadar yanlarından ayrılmayı emretmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r3.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r3.claim: Al-Razi reports scholars who infer from the verse’s purpose that responses beyond physically leaving may be made to unbelievers’ attacks on the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r3.anchor: Fahreddin er-Râzî’nin naklettiğine göre âyetin asıl mâna ve maksadını dikkate alan bazı âlimler, inançsızların Kur’an’la ilgili kötü sözlerine karşı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r4.claim: Following al-Razi, the author understands havd as excessive, playful immersion; he rejects the Hashwiyya inference that deep theological inquiry, proof, and debate are forbidden.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r4.anchor: Havd, sözlükte eğlence tarzında ve aşırı derecede dalmayı ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r5.claim: Some exegetes maintain that the address and command are directed only to the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r5.anchor: Bazı müfessirler, âyette sadece Hz. Peygamber’e hitap edildiğini, dolayısıyla buyruğun da yalnız ona yönelik olduğunu ileri sürmüşlerse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r6.claim: The prevalent view, preferred by the author, takes both the Prophet and the Muslim community as the primary addressees; Tabari, Ibn Atiyya, and Rashid Rida are cited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r6.anchor: yaygın kanaate göre âyetin asıl muhatabı hem Resûlullah hem ümmetidir (bk. Taberî, VII, 228-229; İbn Atıyye, II, 303-304;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r7.claim: The source also records the alternative that the addressees are Muslims other than the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r7.anchor: Muhatabın Hz. Peygamber dışındaki müslümanlar olduğu da söylenmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r8.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r8.claim: The Prophet said he is human and can forget as other people do.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r8.anchor: Resûlullah şöyle buyurmuştur: “Ben, ancak bir beşerim; sizin gibi ben de unutabilirim...”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r9.claim: Forgetting the instruction is excused as a legitimate excuse, but once reminded, one must stop sitting with the unjust.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r9.anchor: Âyette bu tâlimatın unutulması halinde oturmaktan ötürü günahkâr olunmayacağı (zira unutma meşrû bir mazerettir), ancak hatırlayınca artık “zalimler”le oturmamak gerektiği ifade ediliyor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r10.claim: Calling them unjust indicates their speech is not fair, well-intentioned, or truth-based, but aims to insult, belittle, and negate without factual basis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r10.anchor: Kur’an aleyhinde konuşanlara “zalimler” denilmesi, onların konuşmalarının iyi niyetli, adaletli, gerçeklere dayalı olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r11.claim: Muslims may associate with people of incorrect beliefs if they do not insult Qur’anic and Islamic values.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r11.anchor: Allah’ın âyetlerine dil uzatmadıkları, İslâmî değerlere karşı saygısızca sözler sarfetmedikleri sürece, yanlış inanç ve görüşteki insanlarla bir arada oturulup konuşulabileceğini göstermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r12.claim: The Qur’an-mockery case exemplifies a broader rule: leave gatherings where people show hostility through other bad or wrongful speech or behavior, including backbiting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r12.anchor: düşmanlık duygularına dayalı daha başka kötü ve yanlış söz veya davranışta bulunan kimseleri de terketmek gerekir. Nitekim gıybet eden kimselerin meclislerini terketmeyi emreden hadisler de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r13.claim: Zulm includes unbelief as well as all kinds of injustice, unfairness, and deliberate wrongdoing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:68/r13.anchor: “zulüm”, başta inkârcılık olmak üzere her türlü haksızlık ve adaletsizliği, kasıtlı kötülükleri kapsamaktadır

ITQAN:v3p144/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p144/r1.claim: Brevity and expansion are major rhetorical forms; one authority even defines eloquence as the two together.
ITQAN:v3p144/r1.anchor: اعلم أنهما من أعظم أنواع البلاغة حتى نقل صاحب سر الفصاحة عن بعضهم أنه قال البلاغة هي الإيجاز والإطناب

ITQAN:v3p144/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r2.speaker: الكشاف
ITQAN:v3p144/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf says a skilled speaker should be concise where generality suits the occasion and fully elaborate where details are called for; al-Jahiz’s verse contrasts long speeches with a glance sent in secret.
ITQAN:v3p144/r2.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف كما أنه يجب على البليغ في مظان الإجمال أن يجمل ويوجز فكذلك الواجب عليه في موارد التفصيل أن يفصل

ITQAN:v3p144/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r3.speaker: السكاكي وجماعة
ITQAN:v3p144/r3.claim: Al-Sakkaki and others recognize equality as a middle form, neither praise nor blame: brevity uses fewer words than ordinary speech, expansion more when the occasion calls for it.
ITQAN:v3p144/r3.anchor: فالسكاكي وجماعة على الأول لكنهم جعلوا المساواة غير محمودة ولا مذمومة

ITQAN:v3p144/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r4.speaker: ابن الأثير وجماعة
ITQAN:v3p144/r4.claim: Ibn al-Athir and others deny a middle category: brevity expresses the meaning without extra words, while expansion adds words.
ITQAN:v3p144/r4.anchor: وابن الأثير وجماعة على الثاني فقالوا الإيجاز التعبير عن المراد بلفظ غير زائد والإطناب بلفظ أزيد

ITQAN:v3p144/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r5.speaker: القزويني
ITQAN:v3p144/r5.claim: Al-Qazwini’s preferred account treats equality, brevity, and expansion as three acceptable ways to express a meaning; brevity must remain sufficient and expansion must serve a benefit.
ITQAN:v3p144/r5.anchor: وقال القزويني الأقرب أن يقال إن المقبول من طرق التعبير عن المراد تأدية أصله إما بلفظ مساو للأصل المراد

ITQAN:v3p144/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p144/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p144/r6.claim: Al-Suyuti omits equality from the section title because it is rare, especially in the Quran; he notes that the cited example is not equal after closer analysis, since it omits a modifier of الذين.
ITQAN:v3p144/r6.anchor: قلت لهما ولأمر ثالث وهو أن المساواة لا تكاد توجد خصوصا في القرآن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r1.speaker: الْجَاحِظُ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r1.claim: Al-Jahiz says that in the latter half of Ibn Yusayr's verse some words seem to repudiate one another, illustrating phonetic difficulty.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r1.anchor: قال الجاحظ : فتفقد النصف الأخير من هذا البيت فإنك ستجد بعض ألفاظه يتبرأ من بعض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r2.speaker: ممن يزعم
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r2.claim: An opposing account ranks speech by ease of articulation, from extreme heaviness through milder difficulty to smoothness, whose highest degree it takes to be inimitability.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r2.anchor: ويزعم أن الكلام في ذلك على طبقات ، فمنه المتناهي في الثقل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r3.claim: Making phonetic harmony the whole of eloquence removes eloquence from rhetoric and would make sound alone the basis of comparison and Qur'anic inimitability.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r3.anchor: لزمنا أن نخرج الفصاحة من حيز البلاغة ، ومن أن تكون نظيرة لها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r4.claim: Sound harmony cannot account for meaning-based rhetorical virtues such as clarity, apt allusion, sound ordering, simile, elaboration, joining and separation, omission, emphasis, and word order.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p60/r4.anchor: وضوح الدلالة وصواب الإشارة ، وتصحيح الأقسام ، وحسن الترتيب والنظام

BURHAN:v3p442/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p442/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p442/r6.claim: Every Qur'anic use of “wading” is borrowed from wading through water.
BURHAN:v3p442/r6.anchor: وكل خوض ذكره الله في القرآن فلفظه مستعار من الخوض في الماء

RUMMANI:v1p91/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p91/r4.claim: Every Qur'anic use of condemned خوض is borrowed from wading in water and means speaking about God's signs; the metaphor makes their entanglement visible.
RUMMANI:v1p91/r4.anchor: كل خوض ذمه الله تعالى في القرآن فلفظه مستعار من خوض الماء
